title: Take a word out of a char buffer

blocks.text: A String can be built from a char array, `new String(chars)`, or from part of one: `new String(chars, offset, count)` takes `count` characters starting at `offset`. The third argument is a count, not an end index.
Write `word(char[] buffer, int start, int end)` in `Buffer`. It returns the characters from index `start` up to, but not including, `end`:

items: the String is a copy: changing `buffer` afterwards does not change a word already taken.

cases.says: word(buffer, 6, 9) is "you": the third argument of new String is a count.

concepts: A String can be built from a char array, or from a slice of one given by an offset and a count.
